kp.k: Firm moves from third-party tools to proprietary internal AI
kp.d: Gunderson Dettmer announces ChatGD as its first proprietary internal generative AI tool, following years of deploying third-party AI tools, including LLM-powered applications. The firm presents the launch as combining in-house legal expertise with engineering and technology.
qs: The firm has deployed third-party AI tools for years—including some powered by Large Language Models (LLMs)—for a variety of use cases.

With ChatGD, however, the firm has created its first proprietary internal AI tool incorporating the latest in generative AI technology, achieving a new milestone in Gunderson’s ability to marry its in-house legal expertise with cutting-edge engineering and technology.

kp.k: ChatGD supports attorney document work through enterprise models
kp.d: The firm describes ChatGD as allowing attorneys to query and manipulate documents using OpenAI models through Microsoft Azure, with retrieval-augmented generation enabling legal agreements and other source materials to supply query context. It frames the tool as enhancing attorneys’ work as subject-matter experts rather than replacing them; acceleration and enhancement are asserted benefits, not quantified findings.
qs: ChatGD allows the firm’s attorneys to query and manipulate documents using a secure, enterprise instance of OpenAI’s models through Microsoft Azure.
Attorneys using ChatGD can leverage the underlying models and the power of ChatGPT to accelerate and enhance their work as subject-matter experts.
It also gives attorneys the ability to provide legal agreements or other relevant source material as context for queries using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

kp.k: Internal engineering expertise and open source underpin development
kp.d: Chief Innovation Officer Joe Green attributes development to legal engineering and data teams with years of natural-language-processing experimentation. The firm reports that much of ChatGD’s technology stack is open source and that it both uses and contributes to open-source projects, positioning internal technical capability and shared software infrastructure as foundations for legal innovation.
qs: “Our legal engineering and data teams have years of experience experimenting with different approaches to Natural Language Processing for legal applications,” said Joe Green, the firm’s Chief Innovation Officer.
“We built ChatGD using the same state-of-the-art tech stack that many of our clients are using in their products.”
Much of the tech stack underlying ChatGD is open source, and the firm regularly uses and contributes to open-source projects that are becoming foundational to the future practice of law.

kp.k: Generative AI use is conditioned on internal guardrails
kp.d: The firm says its internal AI guidelines permit attorney use subject to guardrails intended to protect client confidentiality and work-product accuracy and quality. Managing Partner David Young describes significant investment in talent, technology and training. These are statements of governance and investment intent, rather than evidence of measured safeguard effectiveness.
qs: As early adopters and legal industry leaders in this space, the firm has developed internal AI use guidelines that permit attorneys to use generative AI technology with appropriate guardrails in place to protect clients’ confidential information and the accuracy and quality of the firm’s work product.

“As a firm, we are making significant investments in AI to ensure we have the talent, technology and training to provide our clients the world-class advice and service that they expect from us,” said David Young, the firm’s Managing Partner.

kp.k: Hands-on AI experience is linked to client advisory capability
kp.d: The firm asserts that developing technical expertise and using generative AI improve attorneys’ ability to advise clients on safe business adoption. Green frames this as an ongoing shared learning process covering both AI-related legal issues and underlying technologies, with broader beneficial changes to work expressed as an aspiration.
qs: Developing in-house technical expertise and experience using generative AI tools is enabling the firm’s attorneys, who are on the vanguard of legal developments in the field, to better advise the firm’s clients on how they can safely leverage AI tools in their business.

“We are on a journey together with our clients to learn as much as we can—both about the legal issues raised by AI and the underlying technologies—so that we can help build a future where AI fundamentally changes the way people work and interact with technology for the better,” said Green.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Gunderson Dettmer claims its internal ChatGD application can accelerate and enhance attorneys’ document-based work and that hands-on AI expertise improves advice to clients.
pts.d: The firm reports launching a proprietary internal application that lets attorneys query and manipulate documents using OpenAI models through Microsoft Azure, with retrieval-augmented generation supplying agreements or other source material as context. It frames AI as augmentation of attorneys working as subject-matter experts, not autonomous replacement. Separately, the firm claims developing technical expertise and experience with generative AI is already enabling better advice on clients’ safe business use of AI. Legal Engineering and Data Strategy Manager John Scrudato characterizes the open-source commons as accelerating innovation in processing contracts, filings and enterprise data. Chief Innovation Officer Joe Green expresses a broader aspiration for AI to change work and technology interactions for the better; this is not a specific forecast about employment or legal-market structure.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The claims rest on the firm’s reported deployment, technical implementation and internal experience, supported by statements from firm leaders rather than measured outcomes.
pts.d: The announcement describes ChatGD’s architecture and capabilities, prior use of third-party AI tools, and years of legal-engineering and data-team experimentation. Green cites the team’s NLP experience and use of a technology stack also used by clients. Scrudato points to participation in open-source projects, including LlamaIndex and the Open Cap Table Coalition. Managing Partner David Young describes investments in talent, technology and training. The document supplies no quantified productivity gains, accuracy tests, benchmarks, client outcome comparisons or concrete examples demonstrating improved advice. Its evidence is a first-party account of capability and experience; the wider positive future is aspirational.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The 2023 announcement presents ChatGD’s capabilities and advisory benefits as current, with permitted use subject to internal safeguards; broader change has no specified deadline.
pts.d: The source reports a launch in the document’s stated 2023 context, following years of third-party AI use and NLP experimentation. Productivity enhancement is described as a capability available to attorneys using ChatGD, not a measured result after a stated implementation period. The application uses an enterprise Azure environment and can incorporate relevant source material through RAG. Internal guidelines permit generative AI use with guardrails intended to protect client confidentiality and work-product accuracy and quality, but the announcement does not specify those controls or a human verification procedure. Investments and learning are ongoing, and Green’s broader future aspiration carries no date or quantified target.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate beneficiaries identified are Gunderson’s attorneys and innovation-economy clients, with internal technical teams supporting adoption and open-source development.
pts.d: Attorneys are the direct users, expected to perform document work faster or better while retaining their subject-matter-expert role. Clients are expected to receive better-informed advice about safely adopting AI and continued high-quality service. The firm describes its client market as venture capital and growth equity investors, innovative companies across their lifecycle, and public companies emerging from the venture ecosystem. Legal engineering and data teams develop the tools and contribute to shared technical infrastructure. Green’s broader aspiration extends to people’s work and technology interactions generally. The source makes no concrete claims about staffing reductions, junior-lawyer displacement, billing changes, client price reductions or access to justice.
